name: Smart Alt Text
author: vigneshkemp

sections.description:
Images without alt text hurt accessibility and image SEO. Smart Alt Text fills the gaps automatically, and it never touches alt text you wrote yourself unless you ask it to.

What it does

  • New uploads: when you upload an image without alt text, it generates one and saves it to the Media Library.
  • Existing images: one click updates your whole library. It runs in small batches with a progress bar, so it works on sites with thousands of images.
  • Front-end fallback: any image still missing alt text gets one when the page is displayed. This covers post content (block and classic editor), featured images, galleries, WooCommerce and page builders such as Elementor.
  • Media Library tools: an “Alt text” column in list view shows which images are missing it, and two bulk actions let you generate or regenerate alt text for selected images.

Smart, readable results

  • Choose the source: the image title (editable in the Media Library), the file name, or the title of the post the image was uploaded to.
  • Clean-up removes noise such as IMG_1234, DSC0042, PXL_20240101_…, -scaled, -300x200, dates, timestamps, WhatsApp/screenshot prefixes and random hashes. IMG_4821-scaled.jpg in a post called “Kerala Backwaters Trip” becomes Kerala Backwaters Trip rather than “Img 4821 Scaled”.
  • Letter case: Title Case, Sentence case, lowercase, or keep the original.
  • Optional prefix/suffix with {site} and {post} placeholders.
  • Optionally also clean up the image title, and fill an empty caption or description on upload.
  • A preview table shows the suggested alt text for your images before you run anything.

For developers

  • WP-CLI: wp smart-alt-text stats, wp smart-alt-text generate [--dry-run] [--overwrite]
  • Filter smart_alt_text_generated_alt( $alt, $attachment_id, $raw, $settings ) changes the result.
  • Filter smart_alt_text_title_case_small_words sets the words kept lowercase in Title Case.
sections.installation:
1. Install from Plugins → Add New, or upload the smart-alt-text folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Settings → Smart Alt Text, review the options and save.
  4. Click Generate alt text under “Update existing images” to fix the images already in your library.
sections.faq:
Does it work on images I already uploaded, or only new ones?

Both. New uploads get alt text saved automatically. For existing images, use Settings → Smart Alt Text → Update existing images, or the bulk actions in Media → Library (list view). Until you do, the front-end fallback still adds alt text when those images are displayed.

Will it overwrite alt text I wrote myself?

No. Only images with empty alt text are changed. Overwriting happens only when you tick “Also overwrite” or use the “Regenerate alt text (overwrite)” bulk action.

What is the difference between saving alt text and the front-end fallback?

Saved alt text is stored in the Media Library and is used everywhere, including the editor. The fallback only changes the HTML sent to visitors and writes nothing to the database. Running the bulk update once is recommended.

Is file-name alt text good enough?

It is far better than empty alt text, but it is only as good as your file and title names. For important images, rename the image title in the Media Library (or write the alt text by hand) and the plugin will use it.

What happens to images named like IMG_1234.jpg?

With clean-up enabled, a name that is pure camera noise is replaced by the title of the post the image was uploaded to. If there is none, the image is skipped rather than given useless alt text.

What happens when I uninstall the plugin?

Its settings are removed. Alt text already saved to your images stays.
sections.changelog:
2.0.0

  • New: alt text is now saved automatically for new uploads.
  • New: choose the source: image title, file name or parent post title.
  • New: clean-up of camera codes, size suffixes, dates and hashes, with fallback to the parent post title.
  • New: front-end fallback now also covers images inside post content (block and classic editor).
  • New: batched bulk update with progress bar, which no longer times out on large libraries; optional overwrite.
  • New: statistics, a preview of suggested alt text, an “Alt text” column and bulk actions in the Media Library.
  • New: optionally fill image title, caption and description on upload.
  • New: prefix/suffix with {site} and {post} placeholders, plus a “Keep original case” option.
  • New: WP-CLI commands and developer filters.
  • Fix: settings were not being saved on the settings page.
  • Improved: multibyte-safe letter casing, full escaping, translation-ready and uninstall cleanup.
  • Tested with WordPress 7.1. Requires WordPress 6.2+ and PHP 7.4+.

1.1

  • Added bulk apply functionality for Media Library.
  • Added settings page with formatting options.

1.0

  • Initial release.
